publications.title: FEViT: Frequency-Enhanced Vision Transformer for Interpretable Handloom and Powerloom Fabric Classification via Spectral and Structural Feature Learning
publications.authors: Humakousar Sangreskop|Uma Mudengudi|Sujatha C
publications.home_authors: Uma Mudengudi;Sujatha C
publications.department: Computer Science and Engineering;Electronics and Communication Engineering
publications.venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Intelligent Technologies (CONIT)
publications.abstract: In this paper, we propose a framework for classifying mulberry silk fabric as either handloom or powerloom using RGB images. Distinguishing between these weaving methods is challenging because both weaving methods generate textiles with highly similar visual appearance, texture, and color characteristics. The challenge becomes more pronounced when fabrics originate from the same material category. Existing approaches rely primarily on visual texture and appearance cues while overlooking the intrinsic structural characteristics introduced by the weaving process. However, the distinguishing features of handloom and powerloom fabrics often lie in repetitive structural patterns, including weave regularity, orientation, and periodic arrangements are used by most models, thereby degrading performance in fine-grained fabric analysis. To address this, we propose FEViT, a dual-branch transformer-based model where one branch learns visual features from RGB images, while the other captures structural information using Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT), which helps represent repeating patterns and frequency details in the fabric. Both branches use Swin Transformer backbones, and their features are combined to make the final prediction. Along with this, we perform detailed structural analysis using edge, orientation, and frequency-based features, and validate the findings across different fabrics such as cotton, milk fibre, orange fibre, soya, and hemp. Statistical evaluation confirms significant structural differences between handloom and powerloom fabrics (p < 0.05). Edge-density and orientation-based descriptors exhibit strong discriminative capability, while frequency-domain representations provide complementary structural information that motivates the frequency-enhanced design of the proposed framework. Although DCT entropy alone shows a relatively small effect size (|d| = 0.29), frequency-domain features capture structural periodicities and weave regularities that are not readily observable in the spatial domain. Experimental results demonstrate that FEViT achieves an accuracy of 98.11%, outperforming conventional appearance-based models and highlighting the effectiveness of jointly learning spatial and frequency-domain fabric representations for loom classification

publications.title: Improving Video Captioning Efficiency Through BLIP-Based Feature Representation
publications.authors: Pradeep Shet|Sujata C|Vishwanath Parameshwarappa Baligar
publications.home_authors: Pradeep Shet;Sujata C;Vishwanath Parameshwarappa Baligar
publications.venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Intelligent Technologies (CONIT)
publications.abstract: Video captioning is a significant activity in multimedia. analytics, in its quest to relate visual data to natural. language descriptions. The aim is to automatically create. significant textual explanations that embody the dynamic conpresence of tents in videos. In this work, a complete workflow is created to transform video content into textual summaries. The suggested pipeline consists of the keyframe extraction, frame- level caption generation, and caption summarization. To iden- tify representative frames, a histogram scene keyframe. detection technique is employed. This method aids in the choice of selection. visual important frames and minimizing unnecessary information. currently available in successive video frames. Each selected keyframe is then processed to generate descriptive captions. For caption generation, two approaches are employed. The first approach uses the BLIP model to directly produce image-to-text captions from the extracted frames. The second approach combines BLIP with T5 to refine the generated captions and improve their linguistic quality and coherence. Finally, the generated captions are grouped and cleaned to remove noise and redundant information, resulting in a more concise textual summary of the video content. We then combine them and summarise using the Facebook/BART-large-CNN model. This helps us generate concise video-level summaries. We evaluate the performance of these summaries against the actual captions using ROUGE and chrF metrics. The results show that BLIP+T5, along with summarisation, produces an information-rich and human-like result. video descriptions compared to using BLIP alone. This highlights the potential of combining captioning and summarisation for scalable video understanding applications. publications.title: LSTM-Based Autoscaling and Scheduling of Pods in Edge-Cloud Environment
publications.authors: Kiran A Chikaraddi|Narayan D G|Sadaf Savanur|Hiremath P S|Amit Kachavimath
publications.home_authors: Kiran A Chikaraddi;Narayan D G;Sadaf Savanur;Hiremath P S;Amit Kachavimath
publications.venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent and Sustainable Electronics & Computing Technologies (INSECT)
publications.abstract: Edge-cloud computing enables low-latency service delivery by deploying applications closer to end users. However, dynamic and bursty workloads pose significant challenges to efficient resource management. Traditional Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) relies on reactive scaling mechanisms, which often result in delayed responses, resource inefficiencies, and degraded Quality of Service (QoS). This work presents a predictive autoscaling and scheduling framework based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) for Kubernetes-enabled edge-cloud environments using KubeEdge. The framework leverages LSTM networks to estimate future CPU and memory usage at both pod and node levels, thereby facilitating proactive scaling decisions. Additionally, an intelligent scheduling mechanism utilises predicted resource availability to optimise pod placement across heterogeneous edge nodes. Experimental evaluation under dynamic workloads demonstrates that the proposed framework reduces response time by 18−25% and improves throughput by 15−22% compared to the default HPA and standalone LSTM autoscaling. The results confirm that integrating predictive autoscaling with scheduling enhances scalability, responsiveness, and resource utilisation in edge-cloud deployments

publications.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Task Offloading in 5G-Enabled Multi-Access Edge Computing
publications.authors: Manoj Madhav Pandekamat|Narayan D G|Sadaf Savanur|Hiremath P S|Amit Kachavimath
publications.home_authors: Manoj Madhav Pandekamat;Narayan D G;Sadaf Savanur;Hiremath P S;Amit Kachavimath
publications.venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent and Sustainable Electronics & Computing Technologies (INSECT)
publications.abstract: The 5G technology offers capabilities such as ultralow latency, high data rates, and reliable communication. This allows for advanced technologies such as smart healthcare services, IoT devices, autonomous vehicles, and data processing. However, extensive dependency on centralized cloud computing causes additional end-to-end delays and congestion. To address this issue, this study proposes implementing an intelligent mechanism for offloading tasks, considering 5G-enabled edge computing and cloud computing. The framework employs a reinforcement learning approach, specifically Q-learning algorithm and Deep Q-Network (DQN) to determine whether tasks should be handled locally or offloaded to the edge layer depending on real-time state of the edge devices and network conditions. This decision-making strategy is quite effective for the minimization of processing latency with much lower energy requirements than the on-device processing approach. In addition to this, the focus on preventing unnecessary offloading of the task results in improved overall network performance. Experimental results demonstrate notable improvements in latency reduction and energy efficiency in 5G edge-cloud networks

publications.title: Simulating the Swirl: CFD Insights into Left Ventricular Hemodynamic
publications.authors: Sinchana S|Uma Hiremath|Sneha Tenginakai|Aditya H S|Karthik Noolvi|Satyadyan Chikkerur
publications.home_authors: Sinchana S;Uma Hiremath;Sneha Tenginakai;Aditya H S;Karthik Noolvi;Satyadyan Chikkerur
publications.venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent and Sustainable Electronics & Computing Technologies (INSECT)
publications.abstract: Understanding intraventricular blood flow behavior is essential for early identification of cardiac dysfunction and assessment of ventricular performance. However, accurately capturing complex left ventricular (LV) hemodynamics through non-invasive approaches remains a significant challenge. This study presents an image-driven computational framework that combines Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) with Statistical Shape Modeling (SSM) to investigate patient-specific LV flow characteristics using high-resolution Cardiac Computed Tomography (CCT) data. Anatomically realistic ventricular geometries were reconstructed from CCT scans and analyzed under physiological pulsatile flow conditions. To improve representation of blood rheology in low-shear regions, the Carreau-Yasuda non-Newtonian viscosity model was incorporated into the numerical simulations. The governing fluid flow equations were solved using a finite-volume-based transient CFD approach to evaluate clinically relevant hemodynamic parameters, including velocity distribution, wall shear stress (WSS), pressure variation, and energy dissipation. Comparative analysis was performed across healthy, aneurysmal, and mitral regurgitation ventricular geometries. Pathological models exhibited disturbed flow structures, localized low-WSS regions, and reduced apical flow velocities, indicating impaired ventricular efficiency and increased susceptibility to thrombus-prone flow stagnation. The findings demonstrate the potential of integrating CFD and SSM for realistic assessment of ventricular flow behavior and highlight its applicability in non-invasive cardiovascular evaluation, patientspecific diagnostics, and future treatment planning.nderstanding intraventricular blood flow behavior is essential for early identification of cardiac dysfunction and assessment of ventricular performance. publications.title: Dynamic Service Function Chain Placement in Edge-Computing Environments Using LSTM and Auction Based Heuristics
publications.authors: Prajwal Ganeshanavar|Narayan D G|Sadaf Savanur|Amit Kachavimath|Hiremath P S
publications.home_authors: Prajwal Ganeshanavar;Narayan D G;Sadaf Savanur;Amit Kachavimath;Hiremath P S
publications.venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent and Sustainable Electronics & Computing Technologies (INSECT)
publications.abstract: The placement of Service Function Chains (SFCs) in edge computing settings becomes increasingly difficult especially when workloads change constantly and hardware resources are limited, more so when applications need minimum latency. Most of the existing SFC placement approaches heavily depend on reactive scheduling or static rules, which are not always effective in such highly dynamic situations. We have developed a framework for adaptive SFC placement that combines decision, based scheduling with workload prediction for a cloud, edge Kubernetes setup. Based on the CPU, memory, and round, trip time (RTT) data collected in the past from the cluster, an LSTM model identifies temporal patterns. Using sliding windows of previous measurements, the worker nodes are categorized as lightly loaded, moderately loaded, and heavily loaded. The model's classification accuracy on the testbed dataset is 96.34%; on the Alibaba Cluster Trace dataset, it is 92.22%. By not relying solely on the present states of the system, these forecasts enable the scheduler to make placement decisions based on expected future states. An auction, based heuristic method is applied to select a suitable node while encouraging stability and fairness among the nodes when they happen to belong to the same load category. The suggested technique is tested under several traffic scenarios and compared with an LSTM only approach and the default Kubernetes scheduler. Experimental results show that the hybrid LSTM and auction, based method can increase throughput by around 22-25% and at the same time have a lower average latency. In general, these results suggest that the issue of SFC placement in dynamic edge computing environments can be more effectively addressed by integrating predictive modeling with fairness, aware decision making

publications.title: Game-Theoretic Proof of Useful Work for Fair Miner Selection and Reputation Management in Federated Blockchains
publications.authors: Girish Kappannavar|Narayan D G|Amit Kachavimath|Pooja Shettar P|Hiremath P S
publications.home_authors: Girish Kappannavar;Narayan D G;Amit Kachavimath;Pooja Shettar P;Hiremath P S
publications.department: Computer Science and Engineering;Not Available;Computer Application
publications.venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent and Sustainable Electronics & Computing Technologies (INSECT)
publications.abstract: Traditional Proof of Work (PoW) consensus protocols in blockchain networks have been criticized for being highly energy-intensive, less scalable, and prone to fairness issues that favor the computations of more powerful miners. To address the aforementioned challenges, we have proposed the development of the Game-Theoretic Proof of Useful Work (GT-PoUW) consensus protocol, which combines the concepts of Federated Learning (FL) with dynamic incentive-revision systems. In this proposed system, every node maintains the capability to train an individual machine learning model, while the selection process for the miners would be based on the accuracy across different models, rather than hash power. This would enable the utilization of the computational power for productive work. To this end, a gametheoretical approach is used for controlling miner classification, update performance, and the dynamic downgrade process in order to effectively prevent malicious miners and encourage honest ones. Experiments reveal that GT-PoUW effectively promotes fairness, which improves Jain's Fairness Index values from 0.7196 in the case of PoW to 0.9537 in the case of PoUW, besides eliminating miner centralization by making the block delivery irrelevant to hashing power. Additionally, an energy-effective and honest plus federated learning approach for GT-PoUW helps boost the current state of blockchain security and fairness

publications.title: An Efficient and Secure Difficulty Adjustment Algorithm for Proof-of-Work Consensus
publications.authors: Nitya Patil|Sumedha Shinde S|Narayan D G|Amit Kachavimath
publications.home_authors: Nitya Patil;Sumedha Shinde S;Narayan D G;Amit Kachavimath
publications.venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent and Sustainable Electronics & Computing Technologies (INSECT)
publications.abstract: Proof-of-Work (PoW)-based consensus mechanisms have been shown to be vulnerable to strategic mining attacks such as selfish mining and block withholding, where rational miners deviate from honest behavior to maximize their rewards. A fundamental challenge associated with these attacks is that many existing solutions are either purely theoretical and difficult to deploy in real-world networks or rely on computationally intensive machine learning techniques. Such approaches often introduce high latency, typically proportional to the number of participating nodes, and are trained on limited attack datasets. To address these limitations, this work introduces a lightweight statistical anomaly detection framework designed to integrate directly with the Ethereum consensus layer. The framework defines a multi-factor risk score, denoted as Rf or k, to evaluate the likelihood and impact of fork-related risks. This score incorporates several key signals, including entropy of block arrival times, chain growth rate, chain depth, and miner diversity. In addition, miner behavior is analyzed through a realtime Miner Score (M-Score), computed using Kullback-Leibler divergence with respect to a trusted reference miner, thereby capturing deviations from expected mining patterns. Experimental evaluation conducted on a private Ethereum test network and within the BlockSim simulation environment demonstrates that the proposed approach achieves a detection accuracy of 95.67% for selfish mining attacks

publications.title: IoT-Enabled Gesture-to-Text Communication System for Speech-Impaired Users
publications.authors: Sinchana Hadagali|Tejaswini M V|Manjula Nayak|Shivani N M|Amit Kachavimath|Maheshgouda Patil
publications.home_authors: Sinchana Hadagali;Tejaswini M V;Manjula Nayak;Shivani N M;Amit Kachavimath;Maheshgouda Patil
publications.venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent and Sustainable Electronics & Computing Technologies (INSECT)
publications.abstract: To assist communication through hand gesture recognition, two significant problems must be addressed: faulty speech interpretation in changing environments and users' inability to control their communication, which lie at a base level. With the help of interactive control mechanisms and real-time feedback, a Gesture-to-Text Communication System based on the Internet of Things (IoT), which can resolve these issues, is presented in this paper. The three biggest innovations around which the system is built are: An interactive interface with Start Sentence and Send Sentence buttons allowing construction of phrases intentionally through gesture sequences; Visual feedback given in real time showing the skeletal overlay tracking that helps the user to position himself during the active recognition; And the word confirmation from both sides whereby the recognized words are first displayed instantly in the serial monitor before the wireless transmission. Besides the hand tracking of MediaPipe, this system also makes use of the MQTT protocol for wireless transmission through ESP32, and the web dashboard has textto-speech features for multiple languages. The experimental evaluation reveals that the system can recognize gestures with an accuracy rate of 92.5%±7.5% and an overall latency of 423±85ms, which is 15.2% better than continuous recognition systems in terms of user satisfaction

publications.title: Hybrid Deep Learning and User-Guided System for Efficient Coronary Artery Centerline Extraction from CCTA images
publications.authors: Atharva Jeevannavar|Parikshith Patil|Mohit Sherkhane|Vedaant Mathereja|Shrinivas Desai D|Kavita Chachadi|Nirmala S R
publications.home_authors: Atharva Jeevannavar;Parikshith Patil;Mohit Sherkhane;Vedaant Mathereja;Shrinivas Desai D;Kavita Chachadi;Nirmala S R
publications.department: Computer Science and Engineering;Electrical and Electronics Engineering;Not Available;Electronics and Communication Engineering
publications.venue: Procedia Computer Science
publications.abstract: This research proposes a new approach to automate the identification of the centerline of the coronary arteries using CNN on CCTA scans. In order to increase the ability of the network to extract important features, the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) is introduced in the CNN architecture to address both spatial and channel attention. The results of the experiments show that the proposed approach performs better than the baseline CNN, with an average OV of 90.735% and an OF of 85.86%, while the baseline CNN only had the average OV of 89. 19% and an OF of 82. 30%. Additionally, the model achieves an average inside distance (AI) of 0.20 mm, outperforming spatial attention (0.36 mm) and average pooling (0.39 mm). Patient-specific evaluations further validate the robustness of the method, with OV values of 91.326% and 89.777% for two test cases. These findings highlight the efficacy of the proposed approach in obtaining precise centerline while maintaining computational efficiency. Future work will focus on optimizing the AI metric, integrating multiplanar reformatted (MPR) imaging for improved visualization, and incorporating plaque analysis for improved coronary artery disease (CAD) diagnosis. Validations on larger datasets is necessary to ensure broader clinical applicability.

publications.title: DABFT: A Novel Adaptive Byzantine Fault Tolerance Framework for High-Performance Blockchain Consensus
publications.authors: Veeramma Yatnalli|Saroja S Bhusare|Guruprasad Konnurmath|Rajani Shetty
publications.home_authors: Praveen M Dhulavvagol;Guruprasad Konnurmath
publications.venue: Engineering, Technology and Applied Science Research
publications.abstract: Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus mechanisms are vital for ensuring reliability in permissioned blockchain networks. However, existing BFT implementations such as Quorum-based BFT (QBFT), Istanbul BFT (IBFT) 2.0, and CLIQUE within the Hyperledger Besu framework face significant challenges, including high resource consumption, limited throughput, and scalability bottlenecks, particularly under complex and high-volume smart contract workloads. In this paper, we propose Dynamic Adaptive Byzantine Fault Tolerance (DABFT), a novel consensus framework designed to address these limitations through Adaptive Quorum Selection (AQS) and Optimized Transaction Batching (OTB). We evaluate DABFT using Hyperledger Caliper, benchmarking its performance against established BFT protocols under diverse transaction loads and operational conditions. The results demonstrate that DABFT achieves up to 30% higher throughput, 25% lower latency, and a 15% reduction in resource usage compared to QBFT. These improvements highlight DABFT’s potential to significantly enhance the performance, scalability, and resource efficiency of enterprise-grade blockchain deployments.

publications.abstract: Blockchain Technology is a nascent technology that possesses attributes such as immutability, security, transparency, openness, and decentralization. Scalability is measured through throughput (transactions per second), space,cost and latency. Bitcoin and Ethereum, which are prominent Blockchain platforms, carry out 7 and 20 transactions per second, respectively. This is much less than popular platforms such as Visa, PayPal, and Amazon, which perform thousands of transactions per second. Therefore, this paper presents comprehensive study of scalability improving techniques for Blockchain and case studies for improving scalability by using some of the techniques. The scalability of Blockchain systems can be enhanced by on-chain, off-chain, and machine learning algorithms.The proposed methodology improves the scalability using off-chain technique for supply chain management and KNN classification for healthcare domain.

publications.authors: Shrushti S Gunjal|Soumya S Malagi|Shantala Giraddi
publications.home_authors: Shrushti S Gunjal;Soumya S Malagi;Shantala Giraddi
publications.venue: 2025 6th International Conference for Emerging Technology (INCET)
publications.abstract: This study proposes a new deep learning-based approach for mean temperature prediction based on weather attribute images using an optimized ResNet50 convolutional neural network model. A dataset of curated diverse weather type images, such as snow, rain, and fog, annotated with corresponding mean temperature labels, was used to train and evaluate the model. The methodology incorporates advanced techniques such as data augmentation and transfer learning to enhance the prediction accuracy and robustness of the model. ResNet50 was further fine-tuned with additional layers designed for regression tasks to enable it to correctly relate image feature space and temperature values. Rotation, zoom, and varying brightness are some of the data augmentation techniques applied as countermeasures against changes in lighting, time of day, and orientation in images. The model achieved a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 2.54°C and a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 3.12°C during testing, demonstrating competitive predictive capability. This research has the potential to combine deep learning with weather imagery for temperature prediction and is promising for areas like remote sensing, mobile climate applications, and disaster management systems where traditional sensor data may be limited or unavailable

publications.authors: Keerthi Vandakudari|Jayalaxmi Naragund G|Vishwanath Parameshwarappa Baligar
publications.home_authors: Keerthi Vandakudari;Jayalaxmi Naragund G;Vishwanath Parameshwarappa Baligar
publications.venue: 2025 6th International Conference for Emerging Technology (INCET)
publications.abstract: Restoring old photos is important for preserving historical and cultural heritage, as these images often suffer from various degradations like scratches, fading, and loss of details. This paper provides a comprehensive comparison of restoration techniques ranging from traditional methods to advanced deep learning approaches. Traditional methods, such as histogram equalization and Fourier transform, focus on enhancing visual quality through basic image processing. Modern methods in the form of inpainting-based GANs, hyperbolic embedding-based generative networks, and GFP-GAN, Generative Facial Prior GAN, rely on semantic understanding coupled with generative modeling to make high-quality results. The need for latent representations, semantic disentanglement, and attentions is shown to be pertinent to the achievement of better performance in restoration processes. PSNR, SSIM, and perceptual quality are all used as metrics for these. Our analysis highlights the strengths and limitations of each approach and their suitability for different types of photo degradations. The findings are not only able to provide clear understanding of the current methods but also valuable guidance for developing more robust, efficient, and high-quality restoration techniques, paving the way for innovative solutions to preserve cultural heritage

publications.title: Automated Brain Tumor Detection and Comparative Analysis Using CNN Model and YOLOv8
publications.authors: Shrilaxmi Byali|Karibassappa K G|Vishwanath Parameshwarappa Baligar
publications.home_authors: Shrilaxmi Byali;Karibassappa K G;Vishwanath Parameshwarappa Baligar
publications.venue: 2025 6th International Conference for Emerging Technology (INCET)
publications.abstract: The correct classification of brain tumors is an important factor in the early detection and treatment of neurological diseases. This paper suggests an automated deep learning-based system for brain tumor detection and classification based on CNN and YOLOv8. The data are MRI scans classified into four classes: Glioma, Meningioma, Pituitary Tumor, and No Tumor. Preprocessing methods, such as normalization and data augmentation, are utilized to improve generalization of the model. Hierarchical features from MRI images are extracted by the CNN model for accurate classification, and YOLOv8 is utilized for real-time detection of tumors. Accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and comparison with state-of-the-art approaches are used to evaluate performance. Interpretability methods such as Grad-Cam are also utilized to identify important regions affecting model predictions. Experimental results show that the CNN model has high classification accuracy, with YOLOv8 providing the best real-time detection. This work is an advancement toward enhancing automated tumor diagnosis and offers a robust tool for supporting clinical decision-making by radiologists. This work adds to the field of AI-based medical diagnosis by presenting a scalable and automatic computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) system for brain tumor classification. The designed system is of huge potential value in the field of reducing diagnostic time, enhancing accuracy, and enabling early detection, thus leading to improved patient care

publications.authors: TaranpreetSingh H Rababi|Shreya Hiremath|Jayalaxmi Naragund G|Sachin Karadgi
publications.home_authors: TaranpreetSingh H Rababi;Shreya Hiremath;Jayalaxmi Naragund G;Sachin Karadgi
publications.department: Automation and Robotics;Computer Science and Engineering
publications.venue: 2025 6th International Conference for Emerging Technology (INCET)
publications.abstract: Human-robot collaboration (HRC) will indeed transform production paradigms in intelligent manufacturing. The aim of this research is to investigate the application and merits of HRC in parallel conveyors and to identify how it may contribute to enhanced productivity, resource use, and operational flexibility. The main issue being addressed is incorporating human-robot collaboration features into the Parallel Assembly Line Balancing Problem (PALBP), which is now referred to as PALBP-HRC. These collaboration modes allow for both parallel and cooperative human-unattended robot operation while enabling the optimization of tasks allocation.For some problems of that hybrid nature associated with PALBP-HRC, a genetic algorithm is proposed to minimize cycle time along with optimal task assignment, keeping in mind the different complex restrictions such as precedence relations, zoning restrictions, and human-robot compatibility for tasks. GA also seeks to maximize benefits deriving from the distinct strengths of humans and robots by using a proper form of task allocation.The experiments show how the proposed GA has demonstrated its capability in solving PALBP-HRC. The cycle time has been significantly reduced with most improved task assignment and flexibility in operations. Thus, the results indicate that human-robot collaboration has been seamlessly included in a parallel assembly line to emphasize not only productivity enhancement but also adaptability in dynamic production environments

publications.title: Leveraging Deep Learning Models for Multimodal Fashion Recommendation Systems
publications.authors: Chandraj Hejmady|Tulip Maurya|Sourabh Magadum|Harsh Goyal|Channabasappa Muttal|Chandadevi Giri
publications.home_authors: Chandraj Hejmady;Tulip Maurya;Sourabh Magadum;Harsh Goyal;Channabasappa Muttal
publications.venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
publications.abstract: This study introduces a novel fashion recommendation system that integrates visual and textual information using advanced deep learning techniques. The system analyzed a dataset of approximately 44,000 fashion items, each having image and text description. For textual data, the system employs bidirectional encoder representations from the transformer (BERT), while visual features are extracted using ResNet-50 model. Comparative analysis revealed that ResNet-50 achieved higher validation accuracy of 0.9895, outperforming other models, demonstrating its superior performance in visual feature extraction. These features were combined through a late fusion approach enhancing computational efficiency while maintaining accuracy. Unlike traditional systems that depend on user reviews or sales data, our approach operates independently of such inputs, making it highly applicable in warehouse-based applications where such data is unavailable during initial deployment. Recommendations are generated by constructing a similarity matrix to identify the top five products most similar to a given query item, reflecting attributes such as design, color, and material. The evaluation showed the system’s high accuracy in providing relevant recommendations with cosine similarity scores exceeding 0.99 for the top recommended products. However, limitations include reliance on pretrained models. Future research should explore more advanced architectures, real-time systems, and additional data modalities to improve the performance across various domains.

publications.venue: Proceedings of the 3rd International Conference on Futuristic Technology
publications.abstract: The detection of lung nodules is essential in medical imaging, playing a critical role in diagnosing lung cancer at its early stages and supporting timely treatment. This study introduces a hybrid CNN-RNN model designed to enhance the accuracy and precision of lung nodule identification in computed tomography (CT) scans. The framework combines the spatial feature extraction capabilities of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with the temporal sequence analysis strengths of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), effectively integrating spatial and temporal information for improved detection performance. Trained on a labeled dataset of CT images, the model’s performance was assessed using metrics such as precision, recall, F1 score, and area under the curve (AUC). It demonstrated significant advancements over hybrid CNN-LSTM models previously used in related fields like Parkinson’s disease detection, agricultural disease analysis, and lung cancer prognosis estimation, which recorded lower precision, recall, and F1 scores. These findings highlight the potential of CNN-RNN architectures for lung nodule detection and their promise in advancing early lung cancer diagnosis

publications.title: Hybrid Approach for Detection and Mitigation of DDoS Attacks Using Multi-feature Selection, Unsupervised Learning, and Game Theory
publications.authors: Amit Kachavimath|Narayan D G
publications.home_authors: Amit Kachavimath;Narayan D G
publications.venue: Journal of Telecommunications and Information Technology
publications.abstract: Software-defined networking (SDN) is now widely used in modern network infrastructures, but its centralized control design makes it vulnerable to distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks targeting the SDN controller. These attacks are capable of disrupting the operation of the network and reducing its availability for genuine users. Existing detection and mitigation methods often suffer from numerous drawbacks, such as high computational costs and frequent false alarms, especially with standard machine learning or basic unsupervised approaches. To address these issues, a new framework is proposed that relies on multistep feature selection methods, including SelectKBest, ANOVA-F, and random forest to select the most important network features, to detect anomalies in an unsupervised manner using agglomerative clustering in order identify suspicious hosts, and to mitigate adverse impacts by relying on posterior probability and game theory. An evaluation conducted using benchmark datasets and validated through Mininet emulation demonstrates that the approach achieves better performance with silhouette scores of 0.86 for InSDN and 0.95 for Mininet. The framework efficiently computes reputation scores to distinguish malicious hosts, thus enabling to rely on adaptive defense against evolving attack patterns while maintaining minimal computational overhead.

publications.title: DISC-GAN: Disentangling Style and Content for Cluster-Specific Synthetic Underwater Image Generation
publications.authors: Sneha Varur|Anirudh R Hanchinamani|Tarun S Bagewadi|Uma Mudengudi|Chaitra Desai|Sujatha C|Sumit Meharwade
publications.home_authors: Sneha Varur;Anirudh R Hanchinamani;Tarun S Bagewadi;Uma Mudengudi;Chaitra Desai;Sujatha C;Padmashree Desai;Sumit Meharwade
publications.department: Electronics and Communication Engineering;Computer Science and Engineering;Not Available
publications.venue: arxiv
publications.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel framework, Disentangled Style-Content GAN (DISC-GAN), which integrates style-content disentanglement with a cluster-specific training strategy towards photorealistic underwater image synthesis. The quality of synthetic underwater images is challenged by optical due to phenomena such as color attenuation and turbidity. These phenomena are represented by distinct stylistic variations across different waterbodies, such as changes in tint and haze. While generative models are well-suited to capture complex patterns, they often lack the ability to model the non-uniform conditions of diverse underwater environments. To address these challenges, we employ K-means clustering to partition a dataset into style-specific domains. We use separate encoders to get latent spaces for style and content; we further integrate these latent representations via Adaptive Instance Normalization (AdaIN) and decode the result to produce the final synthetic image. The model is trained independently on each style cluster to preserve domain-specific characteristics. Our framework demonstrates state-of-the-art performance, obtaining a Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) of 0.9012, an average Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) of 32.5118 dB, and a Frechet Inception Distance (FID) of 13.3728.

publications.title: Brain Tumor Segmentation Using 3D U-Net with FPN and Attention Mechanism
publications.authors: Neha Dyaberi|Bhagyashree Nyamagoudar|Prateek Chittoor|Swadeep Sawant|Channabasappa Muttal
publications.home_authors: Neha Dyaberi;Bhagyashree Nyamagoudar;Prateek Chittoor;Swadeep Sawant;Channabasappa Muttal
publications.venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
publications.abstract: Brain tumor segmentation is a critical task in medical imaging, aiding in diagnosis and treatment planning for brain tumor patients. This study presents an enhanced 3D U-Net architecture integrated with Feature Pyramid Networks (FPNs) and attention mechanisms to improve segmentation accuracy. Utilizing the BraTS 2020 dataset, which comprises multimodal MRI scans (T1, T2, T1ce, and FLAIR sequences), the data preprocessing involved intensity normalization, alignment of segmentation masks, and organization of 3D MRI scans. The architecture incorporates an encoder, bottleneck, and decoder path, leveraging FPN for multi-resolution feature extraction and attention mechanisms for tumor region focus. A combination of categorical cross-entropy and Dice loss optimized with the Adam optimizer was employed during training. The model achieved a training accuracy of 96.16%, Dice loss of 0.0086, a test accuracy of 96.14%, and F1-score of 98.03%, outperforming other baselines, including U-Net and its variants. Practical applications include automating tumor segmentation to assist in diagnosis, surgical planning, and treatment monitoring, improving radiological workflows’ speed and precision. However, challenges such as high computational demands and limited dataset diversity remain, requiring further optimization for resource-constrained environments and validation on larger, multi-institutional datasets. This study highlights the potential of combining FPN and attention mechanisms to advance clinical tumor segmentation workflows, with scope for scalability and integration into real-world medical imaging systems

publications.abstract: Cardiac vessel segmentation is an integral aspect of cardiovascular disease diagnosis and management, yet remains difficult due to the scarcity of annotated medical imaging datasets. This study provides an alternative segmentation framework by employing a Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN) based on a U-Net architecture, conditioned on edge maps that have been generated via Canny edge detection. The generator has been modified to include residual blocks to improve features learning and the discriminator is informed by structural edge information to improve the accuracy of the vessel boundary. The model was trained using adversarial loss and L1 loss which allows it to adequately capture fine vascular structures from single images/masks despite these often being only sparse data. The experimental findings indicate that the proposed method achieves a Dice Coefficient of 84.60 % and IoU of 73.31 % and Pixel Accuracy of 98.22 %, outperforming baseline U-Net and traditional cGAN models. These findings confirm that not only does the proposed model improve segmentation accuracy, but also maintains structural fidelity

publications.abstract: Grasping the dynamics of blood flow is essential for exploring cardiovascular health and identifying irregularities. The research presents an innovative method for simulating blood circulation in microfluidic devices by combining sophisticated modeling techniques with an emphasis on mimicking arterial conditions. The research begins by creating a two-dimensional (2D) serpentine microfluidic model to analyze flow patterns and pressure distributions. The insights gained from the initial model inform the development of a three-dimensional (3D) microfluidic model, enhanced with slice simulations to accurately represent velocity fields and pressure gradients. A crucial element of the research involves developing a microfluidic device that mimics the physical and material properties of real arterial systems. The model features layers that resemble the characteristics of media and adventitia, essential for mimicking the mechanical traits of arterial walls. The final simulation includes a lifelike arterial wall constructed from myocardium material, enabling thorough analysis of velocity profiles and pressure distributions. The research effectively demonstrates the ability to replicate authentic arterial blood flow dynamics in microfluidic systems. This is validated by visual representations of velocity and pressure profiles, highlighting the intricate interactions between fluid dynamics and the mechanics of arterial walls. By connecting biological systems to computational modeling, the research establishes a robust foundation for exploring cardiovascular hemodynamics. The findings emphasize the potential of microfluidic systems for diagnostic and therapeutic applications, significantly contributing to the advancement of both research and treatment

publications.title: Knparaphraser: A Kannada Paraphrasing Model Based on Novel Data Augmentation Framework
publications.authors: Shraajan Gupta|Rachit Malya |T S Sujal |K Robin |Sneha Varur|Channabasappa Muttal
publications.home_authors: Shraajan Gupta;Rachit Malya ;T S Sujal ;K Robin ;Sneha Varur;Channabasappa Muttal
publications.venue: Lecture notes in electrical engineering
publications.abstract: Paraphrasing in the context of low-resource languages suffers from scarcity of large paraphrase corpus, which impacts several downstream tasks where paraphrasing is essential. We propose a data augmentation framework that employs Round-Trip-Translation (RTT) to extend a monolingual corpus into a much larger paraphrase corpus. We incorporate sequence-to-sequence Neural Machine Translation (NMT) model, which integrates multiple decoding strategies at each stage of RTT to ensure that paraphrases are lexically diverse. In addition to this, we publicly release a T5-based Kannada paraphrasing model KnParaphraser fine-tuned on the augmented data. A 100 k sentence-level paraphrase corpus KanPara generated using our model is also released. We achieve an average BLEU score of 0.1967 and a sentence similarity score of 0.8133, evaluating on 1 k sentences. The proposed framework addresses the challenges of paraphrase generation in low-resource languages and contributes valuable resources to the field of natural language processing

publications.title: A Machine Learning Approach for Analyzing and Predicting Hypothyroidism Based on Hormonal Change
publications.authors: Sunitha Hiremath|Sameer Mansur|Ishan Kulkami|Vedaant Mathreja|Saisatwik Madalageri
publications.home_authors: Sunitha Hiremath;Manohar Madgi;Sameer Mansur;Ishan Kulkami;Vedaant Mathreja;Saisatwik Madalageri
publications.venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
publications.abstract: This study analyses the thyroid disease dataset obtained from Kaggle, originally sourced from Garavan Institute in Sydney, Australia, which consists of 3771 cases, to uncover patterns and understand the consequences of this non-communicable disease. The study carried out a thorough analysis of the prevalence of hypothyroidism across age and gender brackets and built a model that would predict the presence of hypothyroidism. The data is cleaned by removing sparse attributes, addressing outliers using the Winsorization method, and handling missing values using techniques like central tendencies. Biasness was removed using Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique, and Age was converted to categories using Data Discretization for easy analysis. It is found that the prevalence of hypothyroidism is higher in females (63.24%) when compared to males (28.44%). And adult women (ages 20–59) had the highest positive test rate (54.70%), followed by elderly women (ages 60–100) at (40.98%). Hormonal imbalances, majorly involving T3 (Triiodothyronine), TT4 (Total Thyroxine), and TSH (Thyroid-stimulating hormone), were predominant factors in hypothyroidism. Elevated TSH and normal T3 and T4U (Thyroxine Uptake) indicated subclinical hypothyroidism, especially in adult and elderly women (79%). Screening is recommended for anyone with abnormal hormone levels, as there is an 82.79% chance of having moderate or secondary hypothyroidism. publications.title: AI-Driven Hemodynamic Profiling: Integrating Computational Fluid Dynamics and Machine Learning for Cardiovascular Health Monitoring

publications.venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
publications.abstract: Accurately capturing unsteady flow phenomena and complex fluid dynamics is essential for understanding and predicting arterial blood flow behavior. This study leverages computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and machine learning (ML) to detect regions of elevated shear stress in the aorta, focusing on the dynamic responses of arteries under varying hemodynamic conditions. The geometric model of the human aorta was sourced from the Vascular Database, which is supported by SimVascular and includes all necessary boundary conditions. Simulations were performed using the Navier-Stokes equations within SimVascular to generate vtk files containing velocity and pressure data. Since these files could not be directly used for ML training, additional post-processing was conducted in ParaView. By applying specific functions, we extracted key metrics such as pressure, velocity, wall shear stress, and other parameters at multiple spatial coordinates. This resulted in a CSV dataset comprising 23,777 points with corresponding attributes for further analysis of high wall shear stress regions. A Random Forest classifier was trained on this dataset to predict regions of high wall shear stress of the aorta by analyzing attributes like pressure, velocity, and wall shear stress, providing precise coordinate-based predictions of areas with abnormal hemodynamic stress. In our analysis, regions of elevated shear stress were detected at 1,288 points, representing 5.42% of the total dataset. By integrating CFD with ML, we successfully identified regions of high wall shear stress in the aorta, enhancing clinical diagnostic accuracy and offering a data-driven alternative to traditional cardiovascular diagnostic techniques. This study underscores the value of combining CFD and ML to reduce reliance on traditional cardiovascular tests, streamlining diagnosis and therapeutic planning while reducing costs and complexity

publications.authors: Indira Bidari|Satyadhyan Chickerur

publications.abstract: The study proposes a novel semi-supervised deep learning framework called Residual Cross-Fusion Network (ResCrossNet) for hyperspectral deforestation change detection. The model processes a pair of hyperspectral images captured at different time intervals over the same geographical area, using identical spatial-spectral feature extraction pipelines. The Spatial-Spectral Feature Extraction Module (SSFM) incorporates residual spatial and residual channel attention blocks to effectively capture meaningful spatial and spectral information. These extracted features are then subjected to the Cross-Fuse Module (CFM), which increases complementary features and reduces redundancy between the bi-temporal inputs. The fused features are integrated using differencing and concatenation techniques to detect both obvious and subtle changes in the forest landscape. Finally, semantic segmentation is performed using the Refined Object-Contextual Representation (ROCR) module, which models object-level contextual dependencies to increase the accuracy of pixel-level change. Its excellent categorization accuracy of 99.6% when implemented with Python showed its potential for accurate and scalable monitoring of forest change.

publications.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive performance evaluation of a novel TCP variant, TCP ENewReno, designed to enhance congestion control efficiency in high-density and delay-sensitive network environments. TCP ENewReno introduces an adaptive congestion avoidance mechanism that leverages real-time bandwidth estimation through acknowledgment (ACK) intervals to dynamically adjust the congestion window size (CWND). Using NS-2 simulations, we compared TCP ENewReno against traditional TCP Reno and TCP NewReno variants across four critical metrics: Throughput, End-to-End Delay, Congestion Window Size, and Jain’s Fairness Index (JFI). These findings highlight TCP ENewReno’s capability to maintain efficient and fair resource utilization under dynamic network conditions, making it a promising solution for emerging 5G and next-generation networking scenarios.

publications.abstract: The growing demand for differentiated services in 5G networks has led to the adoption of network slicing to support heterogeneous use cases such as enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB) and massive Machine-Type Communications (mMTC). Traditional RAN architectures fall short in delivering isolated and service-specific performance. In this work, we present a proof-of-concept ORAN-aligned 5G slicing testbed built entirely using open-source components. The system integrates Open5GS as the 5G Core and UERANSIM for emulating gNB and UE behavior. Two static slices—eMBB and mMTC—are configured using distinct DNNs and dedicated UPF instances to enforce service-level isolation. Performance validation is conducted using iperf3-driven TCP and UDP traffic for the eMBB slice, achieving stable throughput over 50 Mbps in both uplink and downlink. The mMTC slice is simulated using synthetic telemetry-style traffic to reflect low-data-rate IoT scenarios. Prometheus and Grafana are integrated for end-to-end observability, enabling slice-specific metric collection and anomaly detection. Our modular, containerized design enables reproducibility and provides a foundation for future enhancements, including dynamic slicing and AI-driven RAN optimization.

The performance of the GA is assessed against conventional heuristics and random sequencing, with results analyzed using statistical validation and convergence behavior. The approach demonstrates scalability when applied to larger problem sizes, confirming that evolutionary search can effectively adapt to increasing system complexity. Overall, the proposed method provides a robust and flexible scheduling framework for stochastic manufacturing environments and offers a foundation for future extensions involving multi-objective optimization and physical AMR deployment.

publications.abstract: This paper introduces YOLO-OptiMob, a comprehensive pipeline for optimizing YOLO11 models for deployment on edge devices. publications.title: Improving Robustness of DNNs Against Adversarial Attacks Using RAILS, Jacobian Regularization, and Label Smoothing Methods
publications.authors: Sanjana Sunilkumar Kalagond|Rohit M R|Varunkumar Hiregoudar|Shridhar Suregaonkar|Uday Kulkarni|Shashank Hegde
publications.home_authors: Sanjana Sunilkumar Kalagond;Rohit M R;Varunkumar Hiregoudar;Shridhar Suregaonkar;Uday Kulkarni;Shashank Hegde
publications.venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
publications.abstract: Adversarial attacks pose a significant challenge to the robustness of deep neural networks (DNNs), particularly in sensitive applications such as image classification. We propose a comprehensive approach to enhance the resilience of DNNs by integrating three advanced techniques: Robust Artificial Immune Learning System (RAILS), Jacobian regularization, and label smoothing. This combination of methods specifically addresses gaps in existing defenses by introducing an innovative multi-step process through RAILS, which works synergistically with Jacobian regularization and label smoothing to provide a balanced improvement in both adversarial robustness and model accuracy. Label smoothing reduces overconfidence in predictions, ensuring improved generalization, while Jacobian regularization reduces model sensitivity to input variations, thereby increasing robustness. RAILS, inspired by the immune system, introduces a multi-step process involving sensing, flocking, affinity maturation, and consensus, fostering adversarially robust learning in a way that existing approaches do not. Experimental results on the MNIST dataset demonstrate a 46.13% improvement in testing accuracy, from 52.80 to 98.93%, by increasing the number of hidden layers, with a decrease in adversarial accuracy from 96.66 to 88.59%. This trade-off between testing accuracy and adversarial robustness was effectively managed by incorporating regularization and augmentation techniques, ensuring that the model remains both highly accurate on clean data and resilient to adversarial attacks. Finally, we outline potential avenues for further research to extend these techniques to more complex datasets and real-world scenarios, particularly emphasizing the novelty of combining RAILS with established methods for adversarial defense, which provides a robust foundation for future advancements in DNN robustness

publications.authors: Sameer Mansur S|Ishan Kulkarni G|Vedaant Mathreja|Saisatwik Madalageri A|Channabasappa Muttal|Sneha Varur
publications.home_authors: Sameer Mansur S;Ishan Kulkarni G;Vedaant Mathreja;Saisatwik Madalageri A;Channabasappa Muttal;Sneha Varur
publications.venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
publications.abstract: Demand for efficient and accurate billing systems continues to grow as retail environments become increasingly dynamic. This paper presents an advanced vision-based billing system leveraging You Only Look Once (YOLO11), a state-of-the-art object detection mode, in order to enhance the checkout process by enabling precise product detection, counting, bundling and invoice generation. With a robust dataset from Roboflow and a carefully optimized training pipeline, the model achieves superior accuracy (mAP@[0.5:0.95] of 94.84%) and computational efficiency over YOLOv9-t(mAP@[0.5:0.95] of 93.04%) and YOLOv10-n (mAP@[0.5:0.95] of 92.36%), making it well-suited for cluttered retail scenarios. A co-occurrence-based bundling module is introduced, which identifies meaningful product associations from transactional data, facilitating personalized marketing strategies and cross-selling opportunities. Moreover, the model is integrated with a web application to demonstrate its practical usage. This integration of high-speed object detection with actionable customer insights offers a lightweight yet powerful solution for retail automation

publications.title: Resource Management of Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) Enabled 5G IoT Networks
publications.authors: Jayalaxmi Naragund G|Chandrashekhar Yediurmath V|Vijayalakshmi M|Vishwanath Parameshwarappa Baligar
publications.home_authors: Jayalaxmi Naragund G;Chandrashekhar Yediurmath V;Vijayalakshmi M;Vishwanath Parameshwarappa Baligar
publications.venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
publications.abstract: The dramatic growth of mobile devices and the use of user data will result in exceptional difficulties to manage in the current mobile network. It may decrease data quality and service quality of the network. Next generation network 5G and Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) technologies are the desired solutions to manage the resources of mobile networks. Quality of Services (QoS) of end to end mobile network can be provided by combining MEC network with 5G. MEC is an intermediate network between end devices and back bone network. The end device network may include varity of Internet of Things (IoT) enabled 5G applications. MEC servers are processing huge amount data received from the users. This overburdens the MEC servers. Resources like Band Width (BW) management is necessary. So balancing the load of servers is essential for efficiency usage of BW. Service efficiency, system performance, and operating costs have been improved by using appropriate load balancing algorithm on MEC servers. The authors have introduced mobility load balancing in MEC network with 5G to prevent service interruptions due to unequal load. The proposed algorithm Load Balancing Efficiency Factor (LBEF) considers the load on MEC server connected to different neighbouring cells. Edge user equipment of each of the overloaded cells are considered to determine the load efficiency factor. It specifies the sequence of overloaded cells and starts offloading process in them. The proposed method of load balancing on MEC servers in 5G increases the throughput of network with minimal standard deviation

publications.title: Dynamic Tuning of Hyperparameters for Optimization of VGG-16 Model Using Stripe-Wise Pruning
publications.authors: Satwik Kulkarni|Meena S M|Samarth Hanchinamani|Shubhashri Shetty|Diya Patilkulkarni|Prathit Kulkarni|Uday Kulkarni
publications.home_authors: Satwik Kulkarni;Meena S M;Samarth Hanchinamani;Shubhashri Shetty;Diya Patilkulkarni;Prathit Kulkarni;Uday Kulkarni
publications.venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
publications.abstract: The utilization of Deep Neural Network (DNN) models is widespread in various commercial applications, including virtual assistants and chatbots, as well as across diverse domains such as manufacturing, medical, autonomous driving, defense, and security. DNN models excel in addressing pattern-based challenges like object identification, image categorization, and annotation. While these models exhibit exceptional accuracy, their high computational, storage, and power requirements pose challenges for deployment on edge devices. To overcome these constraints, our previous work introduced a novel optimizer called “SparPen,” designed explicitly for filter pruning. It significantly surpasses the current state-of-the-art filter pruning technique called Stripe-Wise Pruning (SWP). With a combined approach of our proposed SparPen optimizer and SWP on a VGG-16 model trained on the CIFAR-10 dataset, our results demonstrate an impressive improvement of 73.4% in terms of memory reduction compared to SWP alone. SparPen employs l1 and l2 regularization techniques, and the hyperparameters can be fine-tuned by choosing appropriate alpha and beta values toward optimizing the model. In this work, we propose a meta-learning algorithm to determine the optimal values for alpha and beta. By leveraging these techniques, we aim to fine-tune SparPen to achieve the best possible results to address variance and variety in the dataset. The proposed optimized VGG-16 model exhibited improvement in accuracy by 0.21% for CIFAR-10 and 4.66% for CIFAR-100 and reduced the model size by 97.66% for CIFAR-10 and 92.91% for CIFAR-100 compared to the reported VGG-16 models. Furthermore, our exploration extended work on the ImageNet dataset. In this context, we achieved a reduction in model size by 80.5% with a corresponding accuracy drop of 5%

publications.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Metric-Based Few Short Learning Techniques
publications.authors: Rakshita Belakoppa|Drakshayani Chalageri|Pooja Karagi|Nikhita Mane|Diya Patilkulkarni|Shashank Hegde
publications.home_authors: Rakshita Belakoppa;Drakshayani Chalageri;Pooja Karagi;Nikhita Mane;Diya Patilkulkarni;Shashank Hegde
publications.venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
publications.abstract: Few-shot learning is essential for tasks involving limited labeled data, where traditional deep learning models often face challenges. This paper provides a comprehensive comparative analysis of four prominent few-shot learning techniques: Prototypical Networks, Siamese Networks, Relation Networks, and Matching Networks. These methods are evaluated using key performance metrics, including accuracy, inference time, and GFLOPS, to determine their suitability for various application scenarios. Our experimental results show that Prototypical Networks achieve the highest classification accuracy of 90.38%, making them ideal for applications such as medical image diagnosis and anomaly detection in industrial settings. Siamese Networks excel in inference speed and computational efficiency, making them well-suited for low-resource environments, such as facial recognition on mobile devices. While Relation Networks require higher computational resources, they offer competitive accuracy and can be utilized in e-commerce for personalized product recommendations. Matching Networks provide balanced performance, making them effective for dynamic environments like real-time inventory tracking in retail. However, challenges remain, including limited dataset diversity impacting generalization, scalability issues with computationally intensive methods, and difficulties in handling intra-class variability and noisy data. Future work will explore advanced optimization techniques, such as quantization and pruning, to further reduce computational overhead and improve deployment feasibility on edge devices. Additionally, efforts will focus on extending the application of these models to real-world challenges, including wildlife conservation through species identification and disaster response via rapid visual data analysis

publications.venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
publications.abstract: Facial Emotion Recognition (FER) and engagement analysis are critical for applications in human–computer interaction and health care. This study presents a robust model leveraging Vision Transformers (ViTs) for emotion classification and K-Means clustering for engagement level categorization. ViTs process images as sequences of patches, capturing both global and local dependencies for superior feature extraction, while K-Means clustering classifies engagement levels into three categories: highly engaged, moderately engaged, and barely engaged. The unsupervised nature of K-Means enables dynamic adaptation to varying user interactions without requiring manually labeled data. Experimental results on the AffectNet dataset demonstrate an 84% accuracy in emotion recognition, with engagement classification validated by silhouette scores exceeding 0.78. This approach introduces a novel methodology to classify emotional engagement, advancing FER systems and providing valuable insights into real-time human behavior analysis

publications.abstract: In an era of rapidly growing information, efficient text summarization is key for extracting key visions. The paper presents a method for generating summary from articles using a Pointer-Generator Network (PGN) combined with attention distribution and coverage mechanisms. The PGN addresses issues like repetition and inaccuracy by combination of extractive and abstractive summarization techniques. The model, trained on the CNN/DailyMail dataset, utilizes tokenization, padding, and advanced optimization methods. PGN outperforms the Bidirectional LSTM (BD-LSTM) across all ROUGE metrics. PGN also scores 16.70% in ROUGE-2, surpassing BD-LSTM 11.67%, showing improved bigram overlap. In ROUGE-L, PGN scores 35.38%, significantly outperforming BD-LSTM 24.97%. These results highlight PGN superior ability to generate more coherent and accurate summaries, making it a more effective model for automatic text summarization

publications.abstract: Computer Organization & Architecture (COA) is a 2nd-year course for computer science students. Recently, 250 students were assessed on knowledge acquisition, critical thinking, practical skills, problem-solving and tool usage through a processor datapath design and simulation activity. Student teams designed an Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) and built a functional processor. For the subsequent batch, the activity was redesigned to focus on individual contributions and peer learning, addressing issues such as weak team formation, inconsistent individual contributions and lack of curiosity. This new strategy aimed to enhance individual assessment within team activities and improve design skills for specific processor specifications. By focusing on both individual contributions and peer learning, the activity aimed to create a more engaging and effective learning experience. Students were divided into diverse teams, ensuring a balanced mix of skills and backgrounds within each group. To prevent issues of weak team formation observed in previous activities, roles and responsibilities were clearly defined for each team member. This approach was intended to ensure active participation and accountability, thereby improving team dynamics and overall performance. Strategies to improve team dynamics included setting clear expectations, fostering a sense of ownership and encouraging active participation from all team members. This comprehensive methodology fostered better collaboration, accountability and higher-quality outcomes

publications.abstract: First-year engineering students often find mastering mechanics challenging, which is a crucial component of mechatronics. The course currently employs hands-on experiments and physical models to teach mechanical concepts, providing a practical approach to learning. To adapt to the needs of the current generation of students, the authors designed and developed an Augmented Reality (AR) technology for teaching planar mechanisms. The primary aim of this application is to simplify the learning process for fundamental planar mechanisms through plane detection technology, making complex concepts more accessible and engaging for students. The AR application augments selected planes with 3D models of the mechanical mechanisms. Users can visualize these mechanisms in dynamic motion, rotate them for a comprehensive view, and disassemble them to understand their internal structure. Preliminary results from a thematic analysis reveal that the application had a positive impact on students. They found the application useful, particularly in terms of visualizing the models, which helped improve their spatial visualization skills

publications.authors: Mangalgouri Kademani P|Yuvaraj Rathod P|Nisha Kubasad B|Ramaraddi Maraddi G|Ashok K Chikaraddi

publications.abstract: This work presents an integrated approach to cyber threat detection and prevention using advanced machine learning and deep learning techniques, combined with a real-time monitoring dashboard. The proposed hybrid architecture makes use of the CICIDS2017 dataset, which contains 682,578 rows and 78 columns and covers a wide range of modern attack types. To identify unusual activity, an ensemble of Isolation Forest and Autoencoder models is employed; the Autoencoder reconstructs typical patterns to identify deviations, while the Isolation Forest focuses on outlier detection in benign traffic. With a 74% accuracy rate, this ensemble outperformed individual models. After detection, XGBoost is used to classify detected assaults into many classes, achieving high precision and recall in multiple classes, particularly for DDoS and PortScan types. A CNN-LSTM model, which has a 99% classification accuracy, is trained on sequential network data to anticipate possible attack scenarios for proactive security. The models were included into a cyber threat monitoring dashboard that enables network managers to make decisions, visualize forecasts in real-time. The system’s performance has been evaluated using measures such as F1-score, recall, accuracy, and precision. The outcomes show how well the hybrid ensemble learning technique works to improve cyber threat identification and prevention in current network environments when combined with deep learning and an interactive dashboard.

publications.venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
publications.abstract: As databases became more complex and widely utilized, the demand for user-friendly systems that allow non-technical users to engage with data is increasing. Current Text-to-SQL solutions frequently struggle with complex operations, especially those that necessitate the capabilities and versatility of PL/SQL, restricting their usefulness in real-world situations characterized by elaborate queries. To fill this gap, we suggest a dual-model architecture based on a transformer-driven sequence-to-sequence (Seq2Seq) framework. Our system effectively assesses the complexity of a specific query and chooses either SQL or PL/SQL for execution, improving its flexibility and user-friendliness. Utilizing the T5-small model, the approach attains 72% accuracy for PL/SQL queries and 90% for SQL queries, showcasing a notable enhancement in managing various database operations. This study addresses the shortcomings of previous research, offering a strong and comprehensive method for database interaction, which enhances the versatility and practicality of Text-to-SQL systems. Our efforts not only overcome the shortcomings of current techniques but also establish a basis for developing sophisticated systems that can handle various database management duties

Furthermore, the proposed approach has significant clinical implications, offering potential integration into computer-aided diagnostic systems to support faster and more accurate detection of colorectal cancer. By reducing reliance on subjective interpretation by pathologists, this model can facilitate early detection, streamline diagnostic workflows, and ultimately improve patient outcomes

These injuries require immediate medical attention to prevent life-threatening outcomes. Manual annotation of rib fractures in CT scans remains a labor-intensive and error-prone process, heavily reliant on the radiologist‘s expertise. We propose a deep learning framework that combines a SWIN transformer-based generator and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to enhance rib fracture segmentation in CT scans. publications.authors: Mohammed Sadiq Z Pattankudi|Abdul Rafay Attar|N Abhishek|Samarth Uppin|Uday Kulkarni|Narayan D G

publications.abstract: Our paper presents a multimodal kannada-to-english translation system based on the mT5large transformer model, fine-tuned on the AI4Bharat Samanantar dataset. Designed to support three input modalities—typed kannada text, images containing printed kannada script, and spoken kannada audio—the system facilitates seamless translation across diverse formats using a unified architecture. For image inputs, Tesseract OCR with the kannada language pack is used to extract text from scanned documents or photographs. For audio, the system employs OpenAI’s Whisper model to transcribe kannada speech into text with high fidelity. The extracted or directly entered text is then processed by the fine-tuned mT5 model to generate english translations. Our approach effectively integrates state-of-the-art technologies in Optical Character Recognition (OCR), Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), and neural machine translation, demonstrating their combined utility in addressing the linguistic challenges associated with low-resource languages. Evaluation of the system yields a BLEU score of 0.5583, a ChrF score of 67.4113, and a TER score of 26, indicating competitive translation quality. The high accuracy across multiple input types highlights the robustness of the system and its ability to generalize across various forms of user interaction. Our research contributes toward inclusive language technologies by enabling kannada speakers to access digital content and services in english, thus supporting broader applications in education, accessibility, and public service delivery. The system exemplifies how multilingual and multimodal AI can bridge communication gaps in linguistically diverse societies like India

publications.title: From Billions to Bits: A Taxonomy and Survey of Optimization Methods for Large Language Models
publications.authors: Aditi Choudhary|Aditya Arasamangalam|Sathvik Kemtur|Sanika Madihal|Sahana Mucchandi|Tushar Bulla|Uday Kulkarni
publications.home_authors: Aditi Choudhary;Aditya Arasamangalam;Sathvik Kemtur;Sanika Madihal;Sahana Mucchandi;Tushar Bulla;Uday Kulkarni
publications.venue: 2025 IEEE Conference on Engineering Informatics (ICEI)
publications.abstract: Physician shortages, rising patient numbers, and urgent clinical judgments are putting increasing strain on health-care systems around the world, especially in settings with limited resources and little access to advanced diagnostic assistance. Large Language Models (LLMs) automate medical documentation, assisting in patient triage, and supporting diagnostic workflows, yet their deployment remains impractical: a 70 billion parameter model requires 140 GB of memory in full precision, inference latency exceeds clinical acceptability on standard hardware, and privacy regulations crutial on-premise deployment that most facilities cannot support. This survey addresses the deployment gap by analyzing optimization techniques that make LLaMA models available for real-world medical applications. We evaluate three quantization methods (GPTQ, AWQ, NF4) that compress model weights to 4-bit precision, and three parameter-efficient fine-tuning approaches (LoRA, QLoRA, AdaLoRA) that enable domain adaptation by training only 0.01-0.1% of model parameters. Experimental evaluation on WikiText-2 and MMLU benchmarks demonstrates that quantization achieves 3.5-4× memory reduction with 94-99% accuracy retention across models from 7B to 65B parameters, while PEFT methods maintain 95-99% of full fine-tuning performance. Combined optimization enables a 70B model to operate within 48 GB memory with sub-2-second inference on consumer GPUs—practical for clinical deployment. Analysis of PMC-LLaMA shows that LoRA fine-tuning improved MedQA-USMLE accuracy from 36.1% to 56.4% using only 0.036% trainable parameters. While identifying important gaps in domain-specific quantization, regulatory validation frameworks, and uncertainty quantification that need more research, our findings demonstrate that the strategic integration of quantization and parameter-efficient fine-tuning increases access to advanced medical AI by allowing resource-constrained facilities to deploy models previously only available to well-funded research institutions

publications.title: A Survey of Knowledge Graph Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation
publications.authors: Sneha Chinchakandi|Yashaswini Mellikeri|Mahesh Khatawate|Amogh Annigeri|Meena Maralappanavar S|Ashish Lodaya
publications.home_authors: Sneha Chinchakandi;Yashaswini Mellikeri;Mahesh Khatawate;Amogh Annigeri;Meena Maralappanavar S;Ashish Lodaya
publications.venue: 2025 IEEE Conference on Engineering Informatics (ICEI)
publications.abstract: Ensuring factual reliability has become a key requirement in Education Technology (EdTech), especially as Large Language Models (LLMs) are being used more and more for better personalized learning and tutoring. On their own, LLMs often rely on static training data, which can make their responses outdated or sometimes inaccurate due to hallucinations. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) was designed to ground LLMs with external data sources, yet most traditional RAG setups that depend on plain text still struggle to provide sufficient context for complex and domain-specific problems. These gaps make it difficult to apply such systems in sensitive domains where accuracy is crucial. This survey studies an emerging approach called Knowledge Graph Enhanced RAG (KG-RAG). It reviews recent works that combine knowledge graphs with RAG models across multiple domains, such as biology, cybersecurity, and education, grouping them by their architectural patterns including hybrid retrieval and graph-based context expansion. The collected findings, such as a 35.2% improvement in student assessment results and an 18.7% accuracy increase in biomedical QA, show that KG-RAG methods consistently outperform standard RAG models. The purpose of this review is to consolidate these developments and highlight open challenges to support the creation of more dependable and domain-aware AI systems

publications.title: Smart E-Waste Classification with Quantized YOLOv12 Model for Edge Deployment
publications.authors: Mohammed Sadiq Z Pattankudi|Abdul Rafay Attar|N Abhishek|Samarth Uppin|Uday Kulkarni
publications.home_authors: Mohammed Sadiq Z Pattankudi;Abdul Rafay Attar;N Abhishek;Samarth Uppin;Uday Kulkarni
publications.venue: 2025 IEEE Conference on Engineering Informatics (ICEI)
publications.abstract: With the growing reliance on electronic devices, the generation of electronic waste (e-waste) has surged, presenting significant environmental and health hazards when improperly handled. Traditional methods of sorting and classifying e-waste typically relies on manual processes that are time-consuming and prone to errors. Our paper proposes a quantized YOLOv12-based automated system for detecting e-waste. The training process utilized a tailored dataset comprising 23 typical e-waste categories, such as laptops, smartphones, irons, microwaves, and washing machines. Evaluation on the test dataset showed that the model attained a mean Average Precision of 0.953 at mAP@0.5 and 0.718 at mAP@0.5:0.95, with a precision of 0.847 and recall of 0.576 across all classes. Notably, classes like light bulb achieved high precision (1.0) but low recall, while classes like washing machine showed full recall (1.0) and strong overall performance. The trained YOLOv12 model was quantized and converted into TensorFlow Lite format and deployed in an Android application. The app performs real-time e-waste detection using the device’s live camera feed, drawing bounding boxes and labels on detected objects. This lightweight, on-device solution can support individuals, recyclers, and local authorities in identifying and managing e-waste efficiently, promoting responsible disposal and environmental sustainability

publications.title: Difficulty In Opening Glass Ampoules
publications.authors: Pooja Gani., Sanjana Patil., Radhika Amashi., Vijayalakshmi M
publications.home_authors: Pooja Gani;Sanjana Patil;Radhika Amashi;Vijayalakshmi M
publications.department: Centre for Engineering Education and Research (CEER);Computer Science and Engineering
publications.venue: Journal of Engineering Education Transformations
publications.abstract: Nurses play a pivotal role in the healthcare sector; we are all well acquainted with this fact amidst the pandemic. A significant yet underestimated task they usually face is snapping off the glass ampoule necks in order to draw the medicine into the syringe during the course of treating patients. This paper ascertains that most of the nurses who encountered this problem were prone to cuts and injuries on their hands due to the sharp edges and medicine spills from the glass ampoules respectively. Thus, the present study aims to address this concern by employing the principles of design thinking as a part of a first-year engineering course; design thinking for social innovation. An active engagement was initiated with the nurses affiliated to a multispecialty hospital situated in Hubballi, Karnataka, India. A keychain glass ampoule opener capable of opening ampoules of 4 different sizes was built as a prototype taking into account the prevention of wounds caused by the uneven edges of the glass ampoules.

publications.title: Detection of Lung Cancer Using Histopathological and CT Scan Images
publications.authors: Aleena Sayed|Nihaal Saunshimath|Fathma Shekh|Sujal Yavagal, Manohar Madgi
publications.home_authors: Aleena Sayed;Nihaal Saunshimath;Fathma Shekh;Sujal Yavagal;Manohar Madgi
publications.venue: 2025 Global Conference on Information Technology and Communication Networks (GITCON)
publications.abstract: Lung cancer is one of the most frequent and deadly cancers worldwide, and it needs accurate and timely diagnostic frameworks to support clinical decision-making. This paper proposes a hybrid AI-based system for lung cancer classification using multi-modal imaging inputs—histopathological images and computed tomography (CT) scans. The system uses both traditional feature extraction techniques (HOG and DAISY) and deep learning-based models with MobileNetV2 to effectively extract both low-level texture and high-level semantic information from medical images. The features are then classified using XGBoost, a robust gradient boosting model known for being highly accurate and robust in classification. The framework employs two distinct models for processing the two imaging modes independently. In them, the deep learning approach constructed utilizing MobileNetV2 provides improved accuracy compared to the traditional HOG and DAISY feature extraction mechanism. The system is modular, scalable, and efficient, and potentially deployable in both clinical and remote telehealth environments. It not only accelerates the speed and accuracy of lung cancer diagnosis but also offers flexibility toward other cancers and medical imaging tasks
